# Gameplay Design Patterns — Björk & Holopainen (the gdp3 wiki)

- Type: LINK ONLY card (academic pattern collection; book © the authors, wiki content per its site terms).
- Sources: book *Patterns in Game Design* (Björk & Holopainen, 2005); the living collection, the "gdp3" wiki (Gameplay Design Patterns project, Chalmers / IT University of Copenhagen lineage): http://virt10.itu.chalmers.se/index.php?title=Main_Page&oldid=27717 (main page, revision permalink as indexed)
- Authors: Staffan Björk and Jussi Holopainen — long-running academic-industry pattern-language project for gameplay.

## What it gives us

- **A shared vocabulary for design intentions.** Hundreds of named patterns (e.g. patterns for rewards, grinding, downtime, resource management, social interaction), each described the same way: definition, typical uses, how it relates to other patterns — which patterns it can instantiate, modulate, or *conflict with*.
- **The most useful move is the relation check.** When a feature proposal names the patterns it uses, the known conflicts come free: if pattern X tends to suppress pattern Y, and the design needs both, that tension must be designed around explicitly instead of discovered in play.
- Use it as a naming layer on top of our own design docs: proposals that say "this is a Downtime + Hoarding pattern pair, which the wiki flags as …" are shorter and sharper than paragraphs of fresh description.

## For みゅけ

Handy when naming what our ambient systems already are (visitor cats, strip events, おかえり ceremony) and when checking that a new pattern doesn't quietly kill the "pleasant to leave running" quality that defines the game.
